task: This is a synthetic exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes as the fixed record: select, organize and phrase the story without inventing additional reported events, scenes, quotations or reporting activity. Write a headline and an explainer of roughly 450–650 words in AP style for general newspaper readers about why the shared water supply at Dovemere allotments is being scheduled by rotating zones. Write from this reporting snapshot as of September 18, 2026.

facts.text: The fictional Dovemere Allotment Association has 60 beds arranged in five water-supply zones of 12 beds each.
The association is introducing a three-week trial of rotating watering periods because its shared tank refills too slowly to supply every zone at the same time under current conditions.
The tank supplies the allotments' irrigation network, not household drinking-water connections in the surrounding neighborhood.
The association's maintenance note identifies simultaneous demand as the immediate operating problem, not a confirmed leak or broken pump.
Each zone receives a separate period within the posted watering window, with the earliest and latest positions rotated weekly.
The schedule is based on the network's zones rather than how long a plot holder has belonged to the association.
Coordinator Lera Moss said, "We are sharing the order of access as well as the water itself."
A plot holder may ask another member to attend during the assigned period, but that does not create an additional watering slot.
Members must notify the coordinator if a zone fails to receive water, so staff can distinguish an access problem from an unused slot.
The association will record tank levels and missed supply periods during the trial but has not published a measured savings result.
Some members working early shifts said the earliest periods are harder for them to use than later ones.
Plot holder Taren Wick said, "Equal minutes are not always equally usable minutes when people work different hours."
The committee rejected a first-arrival queue because it would favor members able to wait at the shared taps.
The rotation does not change the allocation of beds or give a long-standing member priority over a new member in the same zone.
Rain collected in a plot holder's own permitted containers is outside the shared tank schedule.
The association has not supplied crop-specific watering requirements or claimed that every crop will receive an ideal amount.
A proposed larger storage tank would require funding and site approval; it is not part of the current three-week trial.
The committee will consider the operating records and members' availability concerns before deciding what follows the trial.
Printed schedules are posted at both gates because some members do not receive the association's electronic notices.
The site was divided into its present five zones when a central path replaced several smaller access tracks.
The association has not attributed the current supply problem to a named member's excessive use.
The schedule is an allotment operating arrangement and does not announce restrictions for private gardens across the town.

forbidden_additions: A townwide household-water restriction or confirmed equipment failure.
Extra supply earned by proxy attendance or seniority.
Measured savings, guaranteed crop outcomes or an approved new tank.
preserve: The operating constraint and rotation of early and late access.
Equal scheduled periods distinguished from members' differing ability to use them.
Exact quotation wording and attribution when quotations are used.
